newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservative activists want EMU rejected.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservative activists want EMU rejected.

text.p: Motions submitted for next month's Conservative party conference and published on Wednesday show deep hostility among the UK party's grassroots supporters to closer European integration and plans for a single currency.
Only one motion out of hundreds urged the government to keep open the option of joining economic and monetary union -- and that one was submitted by the Conservative Group for Europe.

"This Conference urges Her Majesty's Government to resist further moves towards political and monetary union in Europe," tabled by the Easington constituency association, was typical of the activists' demands.
Several call for a referendum on the issue of a single currency, while many want the government to resist any further moves that would erode the sovereignty of parliament.

Among the more drastic motions are for Britain to withdraw from the jurisdiction of the European Court of Justice, for the abolition of the European Parliament and even for the government to negotiate withdrawal from the European Union.

"This conference calls upon Her Majesty's Government to resist further moves towards a federalist Europe and to ensure that the United Kingdon remains free from Santer's claws," a motion from Salford Conservatives, in a punning reference to European Commission President Jacques Santer, says.
The Conservative conference will be held in Bournemouth from October 8-12.
